raw_output: {"entity0":{"rationale":"This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or Integrator feedback yet. I am choosing a neutral, well-bounded baseline that gives the Integrator a fair platform and makes later evidence easy to read. Sensors: five sensors in a straight row, x = -0.02, -0.01, 0.00, 0.01, 0.02 m, all at y = 0.06 m (ahead of the axle, so the sensors see the line before the wheels reach it, which helps at speed). A 12 mm footprint with 10 mm spacing gives overlapping coverage of the 25 mm tape, so the reading changes smoothly as the robot drifts, and the outer sensors still see the tape at about 2 cm off centre. Body: wheel_track 0.12 m and body_width 0.12 m are mid-range for stability. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, so a body width of 0.12 m is a reasonable margin. Wheel radius 0.035 m raises ground speed per wheel rev, which matters because the 3 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s average. Mass 0.7 kg is light enough for quick acceleration and yaw response while still giving traction. Body length 0.18 m is a neutral envelope. Expected result: the robot should complete the oval and s-bend tracks with a stable controller. The main risk is the slalom, where the tight bends may exceed the 0.06 m off-track limit at high speed.
